import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.ticker as mticker

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/titanic.csv')

# Prepare the data: Fill missing age values with the median for visualization
df['age'].fillna(df['age'].median(), inplace=True)

# Set the aesthetic style of the plots
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid", context="talk")

# Create a FacetGrid to show multiple relationships
# This visualization explores the distribution of age for passengers
# across different classes and sexes, while distinguishing between
# those who survived and those who did not.
g = sns.FacetGrid(df, col="class", row="sex", hue="alive",
                  height=4.5, aspect=1.2, margin_titles=True,
                  palette={'no': '#e74c3c', 'yes': '#3498db'},
                  hue_order=['yes', 'no'])

# Map a histogram with a kernel density estimate onto the grid
g.map(sns.histplot, "age", kde=True, bins=20, alpha=0.7)

# Add a comprehensive title and adjust layout
g.fig.suptitle('Survival on the Titanic: Age Distribution by Class and Sex',
               fontsize=24, y=1.05, weight='bold')

# Set titles for columns and rows
g.set_titles(col_template="{col_name} Class", row_template="{row_name}")
g.set_axis_labels("Age", "Passenger Count")

# Add and customize the legend
g.add_legend(title="Survived", labels=['Yes', 'No'])

# Improve spacing
plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0, 1, 0.95])

# Save the final figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)

import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.ticker as mticker

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/titanic.csv')

# Prepare the data: Fill missing age values with the median for visualization
df['age'].fillna(df['age'].median(), inplace=True)

# Set the aesthetic style of the plots
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid", context="talk")

# Create a FacetGrid to show multiple relationships
# This visualization explores the distribution of age for passengers
# across different classes and sexes, while distinguishing between
# those who survived and those who did not.
g = sns.FacetGrid(df, col="class", row="sex", hue="alive",
                  height=4.5, aspect=1.2, margin_titles=True,
                  palette={'no': '#e74c3c', 'yes': '#3498db'},
                  hue_order=['yes', 'no'])

# Map a histogram with a kernel density estimate onto the grid
g.map(sns.histplot, "age", kde=True, bins=20, alpha=0.7)

# Add a comprehensive title and adjust layout
g.fig.suptitle('Survival on the Titanic: Age Distribution by Class and Sex',
               fontsize=24, y=1.05, weight='bold')

# Set titles for columns and rows
g.set_titles(col_template="{col_name} Class", row_template="{row_name}")
g.set_axis_labels("Age", "Passenger Count")

# Add and customize the legend
g.add_legend(title="Survived", labels=['Yes', 'No'])

# Improve spacing
plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0, 1, 0.95])

# Save the final figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
